subject: gov.policy
name: Data localisation or residency rule
milestone: Nothing on the repository names one
position_end: No data localisation or residency rule is held for the country. The state operator hosts a private cloud entirely in its own data centres, which makes localisation the practical default rather than a legal duty, and nothing states where public or personal data may be held

subject: gov.policy
name: Domesticated geospatial information framework action plan
position_start: no government interoperability framework, no enterprise architecture framework, no data quality framework and no government service bus, on a 2022 structured assessment
position_end: a national action plan to domesticate the UN integrated geospatial information framework, intended to improve integration and interoperability of geospatial information and national data systems

subject: gov.policy
name: Geospatial capacity programme and its framework
milestone: Training extended to a second region
position_end: A multi-year partnership with the regional economic commission is building the state's geospatial capacity. A four-week workshop in February 2026 trained over 25 land, water and environment ministry staff in geographic information systems, remote sensing, land use and land cover classification and watershed analysis using two named software packages with satellite imagery, the second phase of the partnership. A parallel course trained 25 experts drawn from six ministries plus the forestry authority, the statistics office, the cartographic centre and regional administrations, expressly continuing training given in 2025. In July 2026 a follow-on course trained 28 government employees in one region, framed as addressing gaps in the existing information system and improving documentation practices. It sits under a national action plan to domesticate the international geospatial information framework

subject: gov.policy
name: National broadband strategy
status: Not held, on the telecommunications union's own 2019 country table
milestone: Recorded as having no adopted plan
position_end: The telecommunications union's survey of broadband strategies, policies and plans records the country as having none. The table distinguishes neighbouring entries clearly, so the entry is unambiguous. Nothing later on the repository records one being adopted, and the sector rests instead on the 1998 communications proclamation

subject: gov.policy
name: National Policy for ICT in Education and the education sector plan
position_start: Not held
position_end: A National Policy for ICT in Education sets goals for connectivity, ministry systems, staff training and school use of technology. The 2018-2022 National Education Sector Plan aims to develop technology infrastructure and facilities and to provide e-learning options, and names teacher training in technology as essential; the education ministry launched an ICT in education initiative in January 2005 covering teaching, teacher training, curriculum development and education management. The sector plan itself states that incorporating technology remains difficult for want of facilities, equipment and teacher training. Neither the policy nor the sector plan is held as a document, and the profile carrying them is a legacy platform its publisher states is no longer updated

subject: gov.policy
name: Open data policy or portal
status: Not held, no instrument or portal located
milestone: Nothing on the repository names one
position_end: No open data policy, portal or licence is held. What data does reach the public reaches it as survey and workshop output rather than as published datasets: a national population and health survey completed in 2025 with its report scheduled for 2026, and geospatial capacity workshops whose outputs are training and analysis

subject: gov.legislate
name: Artificial intelligence law and strategy
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-31 — a June 2026 legal-status review found no AI law, no national strategy and no institution with a mandate
position_start: no dedicated artificial-intelligence law, no national strategy, no data-protection statute and no data-protection authority
position_end: unchanged, on a review dated 8 June 2026, with an index scoring the government zero on policy capacity

subject: gov.legislate
name: Bank of Eritrea cash-deposit legal notice
milestone: Legal notice issued (~30 Jun 2026) ordering cash held outside banks deposited by 31 Jul 2026 or face legal action
position_end: In force; no definition given of an 'excessive amount' held outside banks, and no enforcement mechanism specified; deposit deadline 31 Jul 2026
sources: 2026-07-02 Eritrea's banking ultimatum - deposit cash by 31 July 2026
note: Reported via opposition/diaspora outlet Awate.com (adversarial framing), with the Bank of Eritrea's own notice text quoted in full; context for the near-total absence of mobile money in a cash-based, under-banked economy under a state banking monopoly

subject: gov.legislate
name: Communications Proclamation 102 of 1998 and the telecommunications framework
milestone: Framework described in a 2025 country profile
position_start: Not held
position_end: The sector rests on Communications Proclamation 102 of 1998, which set the legal basis for communications, the Regulations on Telecommunications Networks and Services issued as Legal Notice 43 of 1998, and a 2003 proclamation establishing the state telecommunications corporation. The repository holds none of the three texts and knows them only through a country profile that lists them; no amendment, licensing regime or regulator is named

subject: gov.legislate
name: Computer-offence provisions of the 2015 Penal Code
position_start: two computer-offence articles in the general Penal Code and no dedicated cybersecurity statute, national response team or strategy
position_end: unchanged: nothing in the window amended the articles or created any of the missing apparatus

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic transactions and e-commerce framework
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-31 — no electronic transactions framework in force; the only texts located are unofficial consultation drafts
position_start: no comprehensive digital-trade legal framework, on a regional trade regulatory profile
position_end: unchanged in law; the only texts addressing electronic transactions are unofficial consultation drafts published by a diaspora legal-reform initiative
note: the draft commercial code and payment systems act are an unofficial civil-society initiative, not a government process

subject: gov.legislate
name: Freedom of information law
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-31 — a UN review contribution states plainly that no freedom of information law has been adopted
position_start: no freedom of information law adopted, against a constitutional guarantee of access to information that has never been in force
position_end: unchanged, and a press-freedom ranking placing Eritrea last of 180 for the third consecutive year

subject: gov.legislate
name: Nationality Proclamation 21/1992
position_start: a nationality proclamation providing the legal basis for nationality certification, with no digital-identity, electronic-identity, biometric or electronic-transactions provision
position_end: unchanged: no dedicated digital-identity statute was located at the probe date

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics law
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-31 — a draft statistical proclamation was recorded pending in 2007 and no later enactment was located
position_start: a draft statistical proclamation submitted to government and still pending, so the statistics office has never operated under an enacted statistics law
position_end: unchanged: no later record of enactment was located at the probe date

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-protection law
position_start: no comprehensive data-protection law, no supervisory authority and no published enforcement decisions
position_end: unchanged, on a verification pass dated 1 August 2026

subject: gov.regional
name: Position in the regional treaty and programme frameworks
status: Not held, the sole non-signatory to the continental trade agreement
milestone: Still the only state not to have signed, at July 2026
position_end: Of the 55 member states of the continental union, only this one has yet to sign the consolidated text of the continental free trade agreement, with 49 having both signed and deposited ratification instruments as at July 2026. That agreement carries the continent's digital-trade and cross-border-data rules. The regional body's digital integration programme, the principal active track on harmonised data governance, cybersecurity and cross-border data flows, states its coverage as seven named member states and does not include this one despite its membership of the body

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional shared digital infrastructure
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-31 — regional infrastructure planning treats Eritrea as a gap to be closed rather than a connected participant
position_start: a regional infrastructure master plan treating Eritrea as a connectivity gap whose interconnection to neighbours or submarine landing points should be implemented in the short term
position_end: unchanged: a later regional overview records that planned cable and data-infrastructure projects lack a commitment to serve Asmara

subject: gov.standards
name: Eritrean Standards Institution
position_start: an autonomous institution as sole national organ for standardisation, quality assurance and metrology, with the international system of units adopted as the legal measurement system
position_end: unchanged: nothing in the window amended the proclamation or recorded a digital or data standard made under it

subject: gov.discourse
name: Non-governmental contribution to national policy
position_start: an education ICT policy committing the state to narrowing the digital divide and to access for all citizens regardless of gender or location
position_end: a first national development plan described as drafted through participatory consultation, and technical geodesign workshops in Asmara bringing government, academic, private-sector and non-governmental participants together

subject: gov.discourse
name: Public discussion of government policy
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-31 — no independent press, permitted civil society or public forum in which policy could be argued
position_start: a UN commission finding that the state systematically silences criticism, with surveillance and punishment producing self-censorship in private settings
position_end: unchanged, and a press-freedom ranking placing Eritrea last of 180 for the third consecutive year

subject: finance.budget
name: Investment climate and the institutions for mobilising finance
status: Discontinued, the investment centre dormant and the investment law suspended
position_end: The external country assessment establishes that the investment centre created in 1998 is dormant, that the 1994 investment law is effectively suspended, and that mobilisation of non-state finance happens only through opaque party-negotiated deals rather than through a functioning private or blended-finance institution. There is no domestic budget line for digital transformation on the repository and no instrument through which one could be raised

subject: finance.mou
name: African Development Bank financial-sector modernisation dialogue
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: a bank delegation mission in April 2026 reviewing continued dialogue on a prospective financial sector modernisation project covering data systems

subject: finance.new
name: GPE System Transformation and System Capacity Grants
milestone: US$14.02m committed through UNICEF as grant agent, April 2024
position_start: Committed to a foundational-learning programme including work on the education management information system (2025-08)
position_end: US$14.02m to the education ministry through UNICEF as grant agent, for a foundational-learning reform programme including strengthening of the education management information system

subject: finance.new
name: UNDP 'Economic & Social Data Development Eritrea' grant (IATI 00099544)
milestone: UNDP commits US$1,676,837 grant to the Government of Eritrea / National Statistics Office
position_end: Committed 2019, end year 2026 per IATI record; funds NSO statistical-capacity building, including the EPHS 2025 survey under the same D4D programme (see data.statistics)

subject: infra.connect
name: EriTel national network expansion programme
milestone: Minister reports 184 towers installed, ~90% geographic mobile coverage, service 'reaching 4G level' (government claim)
position_end: 184 towers and accessories installed; landline renovation in six named towns plus the Naval Force Base; ~73km new cable laid; internet bandwidth risen to ~1,536 Mbps over the past decade; 35bn+ Nakfa cumulative investment claimed
sources: 2026-05-19 Eritrea substantial investment in communication service expansion
note: Minister's own figures (state media); geographic coverage is not population coverage and is not independently verifiable

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet exchange points
status: Not held, none active on the exchange registry
position_end: The exchange tracker states directly that there are no active internet exchange points in the country and none listed in the peering database. All domestic traffic between networks therefore leaves the country and returns, over an international transit that runs on geostationary satellite. An exchange at the capital is among the proposals in a diaspora policy piece and in no government document

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile broadband affordability
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period
position_end: an entry-level mobile broadband basket at 85% of monthly gross national income per head, against a 2% affordability benchmark
note: no later Eritrea-specific affordability figure was located at the probe date

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile network coverage and internet use
milestone: ITU 2023 coverage figures, carried in a 2025 country profile
position_start: Not held
position_end: A country profile carries the 2023 international telecommunication union figures: 85% of the population covered by a mobile-cellular network, 35% by at least third-generation service and 0% by at least fourth-generation, with fixed broadband subscriptions effectively negligible. It puts internet use at about 27% of the population on a separate estimate. The same profile records that the market is dominated by one operator and that, with no public submarine cable landing station, its internet connectivity relies on geostationary satellite links. These are first coverage figures for this repository with nothing earlier behind them

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink satellite internet service
milestone: Starlink's own coverage-availability map lists Eritrea 'No planned launch date'
position_end: No planned launch date (17 Jul 2026); one of seven African states with no announced timeline, all in Northern Africa/the Horn; no evidence found of a licence application or refusal

subject: infra.connect
name: Submarine fibre-optic cable landing
milestone: Cable industry calls Eritrea a 'black hole' that does not answer landing requests; still cable-less as of Apr 2026
position_start: No cable landing; state did not respond to Red Sea route approaches from cable firms (2024)
position_end: No cable landing; not party to UNCLOS; EriTel's international transit runs on geostationary satellite
sources: 2024-06-10-cable-firms-eye-eritrea-red-sea-houthi-attacks|2026-04-16 The Long View - What ICT4D did for Africa and why that deep past matters for today
note: Submarine Networks industry registry lists Eritrea as the sole non-landing state among Africa's 38 coastal states, but that count is itself undated (adjacent stats stamped end-2019)

subject: infra.store
name: Proposed national digital infrastructure agenda
status: Planned, a diaspora policy proposal with no government adoption
position_end: A long-form policy analysis proposes a national digital infrastructure and governance agenda: a submarine cable landing at two named ports, redundant fibre, an exchange point at the capital, domestic data-centre capacity, diversified technology partners, diaspora technical mobilisation and a national digital infrastructure authority. It is an independent diaspora-oriented outlet rather than a constituted think tank or academic department, and no evidence of government adoption of any part of it is held

subject: infra.store
name: State operator's private cloud service
milestone: Service page published on the operator's site
position_end: The state operator offers a platform-as-a-service private cloud hosted entirely in its own data centres, in three subscription tiers of 100, 250 and 500 gigabytes of storage for 20, 50 and 100 users, each with a stated 90 per cent uptime service level and a recovery-time objective of up to six days. It is the clearest primary evidence that domestic provider-hosted storage capacity exists. No aggregate national capacity figure, facility count or location is published, and a six-day recovery objective is the measure of what backup means here

subject: infra.energy
name: Decentralised mini-grid architecture
milestone: Head of state sets out the architecture
position_end: The head of state's interview formalises a decentralised national energy architecture: twelve independent mini-grid power centres targeting 360 MW, each growing to 30 MW, to be interconnected into a national grid eventually reaching about 2,000 MW, framed explicitly as a response to the inadequacy of the existing centralised grid. It is a stated architecture with no site, cost, financier or timetable published against it

subject: infra.energy
name: Interconnected grid capacity and reliability
milestone: Financier's project appraisal states the position
position_end: The financier's appraisal, prepared with the energy and mines ministry and the electricity corporation, states the position: interconnected grid installed capacity 157 MW with only 52 MW reliably available against current demand of 74.3 MW, renewables at 6 MW, and generation almost entirely reliant on imported diesel through ageing breakdown-prone infrastructure. A grid delivering two thirds of the demand placed on it is the constraint every digital system in the country sits behind, and no data centre's supply arrangement, tariff or water requirement is published anywhere

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National cybersecurity strategy
milestone: Absence recorded in a 2025 country profile
position_start: Not held
position_end: A country profile records that Eritrea has no public national cybersecurity strategy. It also records that in May 2024 the government publicly announced that the country's internet system had been hit by what it called a massive cyberattack, repelled without service interruption. No incident detail, response body, computer emergency response team or subsequent statement is on record, and the repository holds nothing else at all on cybersecurity for this country

subject: dpi.exchange
name: ASYCUDA World customs platform
position_start: 2007-era paper-based customs software (no ASYCUDA)
position_end: ASYCUDA World implemented with UNDP support, full source-code transfer to the Eritrean government for national ownership
sources: 2026-01-08 Eritrea launches ASYCUDA World digital customs system

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Vulnerability database for social protection
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period
position_end: a vulnerability database established in the labour and welfare ministry to collect and analyse gender-segregated data on persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups
note: the report does not state that this database exchanges data with any other system

subject: dpi.id
name: Customer identification duty on financial institutions
position_end: The anti-money-laundering proclamation requires financial institutions to establish customer due-diligence and identification policies for every account and transaction relationship, with the central bank as supervisory authority. Regional assessment describes the framework as requiring the identity card as the accepted customer-identification document in practice, which is the clearest standing example of the national identity credential being consumed by a system other than the register that issues it

subject: dpi.id
name: Issuance and standing of the national identity card
status: Implemented, most holders on handwritten cards
position_end: The identity card is issued by the immigration and nationality department at a fee of 100 nakfa. A plastic card with a hologram and fingerprint was introduced late in 2015 for those aged 18 and over, and the standing position is that very few new cards are in circulation, most people still hold the old handwritten cards, and there is a long application backlog. A credential most of whose holders carry a handwritten version is the repository's answer on both maintenance and issuance from birth

subject: dpi.id
name: National foundational digital ID
milestone: Global Digital Identity Index profile finds no operational foundational ID; sets out the barriers a future system would face
position_end: No operational foundational digital ID; barriers profiled: low connectivity/mobile penetration, limited digital infrastructure, telecom monopoly (EriTel), weak civil registration. The credential the country does issue is separately recorded: a national identity card first issued in 1992, handwritten until 2014, now being replaced by an electronic card

subject: dpi.id
name: National identity card and its issuance
position_start: Not held
position_end: Identity cards are issued by the Department of Immigration and Nationality, were first issued in 1992 and were handwritten until 2014. Applicants submit a supporting letter from their municipality administration, a birth certificate and proof of citizenship to one of twelve branch offices, which forward the application to headquarters in the capital for approval; a replacement costs 100 nakfa, the old card being surrendered and destroyed. The card carries name, sex, date and place of birth and an identification number in the two official languages. A newer electronic card carries a laser-engraved photograph, the holder's fingerprint and a unique serial number for tracing a lost card. Citizens aged 18 and over are required to hold one, and children of Eritrean parents may hold an underage card. No issuance volume, coverage rate or database behind the card is on record
note: The fullest account is a 2018 country-of-origin research response; the 2024 consular page confirms the requirement but adds no system detail

subject: dpi.pay
name: Banked population and the structure of the financial system
position_start: Not held
position_end: More than 70% of Eritreans are estimated to remain unbanked. The financial system is highly centralised on a small number of state-owned banks, one of which provides the majority of retail banking, which the account links to limited competition, minimal innovation and heavy reliance on manual processes. Mobile penetration was put at just under 60% of population in 2022, ranked 191st of 209 economies. The figures are a trade publication's estimates rather than a central bank or survey series, and no official financial inclusion measurement for the country is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Isolation of the financial system from cross-border rails
position_end: The regional peer assessment, following an on-site visit in July and August 2024, states that the financial system is state-owned and offers simple and less sophisticated services with no automatic teller machines, debit or credit cards or internet banking, that the financial intelligence unit is not yet operational, and that the sector remains largely disconnected from the global financial system. Cross-border digital payment is not partially available here; the instruments it would run on do not exist

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile money / digital payments service
status: Not held, searched 2026-03-30 — a sector account of the country's fintech position names no mobile money or digital payments service
position_start: no mobile money or digital payment service on the record
position_end: A trade account of the country's fintech position in 2026 records that more than 70% of Eritreans remain unbanked, that the financial system is highly centralised on a small number of state-owned banks with one providing the majority of retail banking, and that online banking, cash machines and mobile financial applications remain largely absent, so cash continues to dominate economic activity. Total online commerce is estimated at under US$10m a year. No mobile money or digital payments service is named at any point
note: No named mobile-money or digital-payments system on file; base holds only the cash-based, under-banked context around the Bank of Eritrea deposit ultimatum (see gov.legislate)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payment systems and the financial sector's standing
milestone: Financier names payment systems a priority for 2025-2027
position_end: The financier's country strategy documents an underdeveloped financial sector as a binding constraint on growth and names strengthening institutional and regulatory frameworks, particularly payment systems, as an explicit priority for 2025 to 2027. It is an assessment that foundational work is required rather than a report of an established uptake figure; no financial-access survey figure for the country is held, and more than 70 per cent of the population is estimated to remain unbanked

subject: dpi.registry
name: Business Information Register
position_start: a statutory business information register maintained by the trade ministry, covering trade, manufacturing, services, fisheries and commercial farming, with specified fields and annual reporting
position_end: unchanged and still manual: an external assessment records no business-registration website and registration through six government offices

subject: dpi.registry
name: Cadastral Office and land register
position_start: a cadastral office responsible for registering all land, rights over land and transfers of property, on a tenure system in which all land belongs to the state
position_end: unchanged: the founding law does not establish the register's operational extent and nothing later on the repository does either

subject: dpi.registry
name: Civil registration of births and its coverage
milestone: Completeness fields returned blank in the 2025 reporting-year questionnaire
position_start: Not held
position_end: The country's return to the United Nations vital statistics questionnaire for reporting year 2025 leaves the completeness fields for birth and death registration blank, so no registration completeness estimate is reported at all. The only description the repository holds of the system's shape is twenty-four years old: birth registration then ran under a transitional civil code in eight named urban areas only and not in rural areas, was optional rather than obligatory even there, was kept for administrative purposes with no statistical data retained, and the urban offices did not know their own annual registered births. The same account records that no proper registration system or population census had been conducted before or since independence in 1991
note: The structural account is from 2002 and is stated as such; the 2025 questionnaire establishes only that no completeness figure is reported

subject: dpi.registry
name: Disability and social protection policy framework
position_end: The government's own periodic report describes the framework: a national policy for persons with disabilities revised in 2021 with a translation in 2023, accession to the disability rights convention on 20 December 2024, and a national social protection policy and strategic plan for 2022 to 2026. The register behind it is a vulnerability database in the labour and welfare ministry collecting gender-segregated data on persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. The external committee's concluding observations of July 2026 record the state's position that it hosts no refugee, asylum-seeking or internally displaced children and recommend it establish status-determination procedures and contingency plans

subject: dpi.registry
name: National address and postcode system
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-31 — Eritrea does not appear on the postal union's list of countries operating a postcode system
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period
position_end: no national postcode system, on the postal union's own reference list

subject: dpi.registry
name: Voter register
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-31 — the electoral law provides for a register but no national election has been held under it
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period
position_end: an electoral law providing for an independent commission to prepare the register, issue voting cards and publish it for inspection, with nothing recording a register ever compiled
note: the hosted text is undated; the date is a proxy for the page access, not the law's promulgation

subject: dpi.registry
name: Zoba-level digital population registers
position_start: six separate regional digital population registers in place since 2001, with no central national register; residence and family identity cards are printed extracts of them
position_end: the same decentralised registers, with a five-year civil registration and vital statistics plan for 2024-2028 recognised by a regional treaty body

subject: dpi.mis
name: Analytical support to the education management information system
position_end: A request for proposal seeks a consultant for analytical support to the education management information system, responding to identified weaknesses in its analysis, gender disaggregation and data use, and requiring analysis of teacher deployment and attrition by gender and location, ministry capacity-building workshops and a validated policy brief. It is targeted procurement against named weaknesses in a system the government's own programme document describes as largely paper-based

subject: dpi.mis
name: Data systems for child protection and social services
position_end: The children's rights committee's concluding observations, adopted at the end of January 2025, are the repository's most recent external assessment of the data systems behind social protection and child services. They also record that the 2015 penal, civil and procedural codes are not yet in force, the amended transitional penal code remaining the operative law, which leaves the country without an operative statute reaching computer or electronic offences

subject: dpi.mis
name: Education and teacher management information systems
position_start: an education management information system used to identify barriers and prioritise reforms, with a teacher management information system named as a planned enabling instrument
position_end: the same, with a ministry delegation attending a regional workshop to learn teacher management information system practice

subject: dpi.mis
name: Eritrea Integrated Tax Administration System
position_start: Not held
position_end: The finance ministry invited sealed bids in September 2023 for the supply, installation and configuration of an integrated tax administration system with its hardware and IT equipment, under a development bank governance-sector project. The scope includes implementation services with training, change management and quality assurance; cleaning, validation and migration of legacy data from the current system; deployment from a main production site to other locations in the capital and to every inland revenue office in the zobas; data replication and business continuity for disaster recovery; and support under a service level agreement. No contract award, go-live date or operating account has followed on the record, three years on

subject: dpi.mis
name: Integrated tax administration system implementation
milestone: Software and hardware delivered and installed
position_end: The financier's own supervision report on the tax administration system records software and hardware delivery and installation complete, the first release's requirements specification complete, disbursement at 67.21 per cent as of June 2026, and implementation progress rated satisfactory. It is the single most authoritative current statement of the system's standing, and the taxpayer register it would carry has no published size at any date

subject: dpi.mis
name: Justice sector management information system
status: Not held, no platform named in the ministry's own review
milestone: Ministry activity assessment names technology without a system
position_end: The justice ministry's own 2024 activity review and 2025 plan names advancing the use of technology among its priority programmes and does not name or describe any court case-management or justice management information system. It is the best available statement of the sector's standing, and what it establishes is that no such system is on the record

subject: dpi.mis
name: National Health Information System
position_start: an established national health information system with a district platform rolled out to about 40% of secondary-level and above facilities, and interoperability between systems rated not there
position_end: the same system, with genomic sequencing capacity built at the national laboratory since 2024 and applied nationally to malaria and antimicrobial-resistance surveillance for the first time

subject: dpi.mis
name: Standing of the education management information system
milestone: Government programme document states the position
position_end: The government's own programme document states that an education management information system exists, that data collection remains largely paper-based and manual, and that connectivity, equipment, staffing, analytical capacity and system design are all inadequate, the system to be strengthened through improved routine collection, processing, storage and use. The ministry publishes annual reports from it in hard copy and electronic form. The programme carries a system transformation grant of US$11.82 million and a system capacity grant of US$2.2 million

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Online government services
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-31 — the customs platform is the only operating government digital system on the repository and it is internal, not citizen-facing
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period
position_end: one internal system — a customs platform on an intranet architecture — and no citizen-facing online service
note: the e-government survey's country-level index values for Eritrea are not present in the captured text

subject: digital.localgov
name: ICT at sub-national government offices
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period
position_end: a central ministry network and internet server with six regions and 30 of 55 sub-regions on dial-up, and no computer at all in 25 of 55 sub-regional offices
note: this is the most recent assessment of sub-national office ICT located; it is more than two decades old

subject: digital.localgov
name: Training on documentation, archives and records digitisation
position_end: One regional administration, with the national research and documentation centre, trained 64 employees of local institutions in document organisation, preservation, evaluation and digital document management in September 2025. In July 2026 a second region's administration and its sectoral branches took geographic information systems training framed as addressing gaps in the existing information system and improving documentation practices. Both are capacity-building rather than an operating digitised-records system, against a standing position of a central ministry network with 30 of 55 sub-regions on dial-up and no computer at all in 25 of them

subject: digital.rural
name: Digitisation of health data capture
position_end: A national workshop of 14 and 15 October 2025 introduced a smartphone application for reporting adverse events following immunisation and adverse drug reactions, with over 60 participants including national and zonal focal points, regulatory officers and information technology specialists, framed explicitly as enabling transition from paper-based to digital adverse-event reporting. An independent long-form account reports the formal introduction of a digital health policy and a health information and communications technology strategic plan for 2026 to 2030; it is not yet corroborated by an official health ministry or health agency source

subject: digital.rural
name: Police station record systems and their reach
milestone: Nationwide maintenance training for police members
position_end: The state's own national human rights report records that the police force had established police centres in 53 sub-regions and 34 further stations in remote areas, and that a computerised data system enabled systematic management of crime records, vehicle registration, traffic violations and financial and personnel management. The report does not link that system to the remote stations specifically. In June 2026 the police trained members drawn from all stations across the country and headquarters in computer maintenance, printer maintenance and computer networking, which indicates stations were expected to maintain equipment and network functions without establishing that electronic record capture was live at station level

subject: tech.ai
name: Agricultural expert system
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period
position_end: an expert system described by the agriculture ministry as part of artificial intelligence, giving farmers guidance when extension workers are unavailable, inside an information system division established in 2019

subject: tech.ai
name: Control of artificial-intelligence abuse
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-31 — no domestic law, regulator or takedown route exists; the only response on the record is external fact-checking
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period

subject: tech.ai
name: Eri-Chat offline AI app
milestone: Q&A profile of developer Naod Goitom Isaac; app launched April 2025, showcased at Asmara UN Day event, Oct 2025
position_start: Live since April 2025 (pre-window launch), offline open-source-AI app storing conversation data locally on-device
position_end: Live; showcased at Asmara UN Day event (24 Oct 2025) to ambassadors, UN officials and diplomats; English-only, local-language support pending (insufficient training data)
note: Built by a Ministry of Information software developer; a rare concrete Eritrean AI/innovation data point. Launch dated to month only (April 2025)

subject: tech.industry
name: Communications Proclamation 102 of 1998 as the production framework
position_end: The founding communications-sector law establishes the ministry's communications department as sole sector regulator over telecommunications, broadcasting and post, and sets as an objective the establishment of technical standards and promotion of the development of the country's communications capabilities, industries and skills. It is the legal basis for any national production capacity in the sector, through operator licensing, equipment supplier and installer permits and a rural telecommunications fund. Twenty-eight years on, no manufacturer, assembler or licensed equipment supplier is named on the repository

subject: tech.innovate

milestone: Five applications released, described in a 2026-08-15 interview
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Five Tigrinya-language mobile applications released by a self-organised software collective - literacy, puzzle, cultural-heritage and arithmetic tools built to the national curriculum - with a stated plan to extend to Eritrea's eight other national languages; no download count, distribution channel or funding source is stated
note: a self-organised private collective rather than a state programme, described in the state information ministry's own interview

position_start: Not held
position_end: An Eritrean virtual-reality project renders traditional Hidmo housing and other heritage settings in three dimensions (2026-09)

position_end: a hub established in 2023 by the national youth union running three levels of six-month technical training in electronics, Python, Scratch, robotics and soldering, mainly for secondary students

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Digital training for government employees
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period
position_end: one regional vocational-training activity in computer technology and networking for 108 government employees and force members, 63 of them women
note: no standing nationwide civil-service digital-skills scheme was located

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital training in secondary education and outside it
milestone: Private institute's account of its throughput
position_end: The education ministry's own status overview names information technology in education as a distinct programme area within secondary and general education alongside technical and vocational training and curriculum reform; the captured text reaches page eleven and not that section, so the repository holds the programme's existence and not its content. Outside the school system a private technology training institute with four branches across two cities graduates roughly 700 young people a year from its computer technology, electrical and electronic and audio-visual departments, with about 50 graduates in 2026 from new introductory artificial intelligence courses, some already producing commercial animation

subject: capacity.training
name: Graduates entering the technology workforce
position_end: The principal engineering college graduated 297 students at its nineteenth commencement, 25 per cent of them women, comprising 289 first degrees including computer science and engineering and eight diplomas including computer application technology and computer hardware and networking technology. Alongside it a private institute graduates roughly 700 a year from technology departments, with named alumni opening their own technology shops. Those are the two pipelines the repository can count; no measure of where either cohort goes is published

subject: capacity.training
name: Mai Nefhi College of Engineering and Technology
position_start: a college offering computer engineering degrees and computer, communication and electrical technology diplomas within the national institute of technology
position_end: the same college showing 26 research papers and engineering solutions, 32 illustrations and 29 demonstrations at its engineering day, from 1,694 students of whom 39% are women

subject: capacity.research
name: Science and technology research institutions
position_end: The 2002 proclamation establishes a national science and technology council chaired by the head of state, a science and technology development agency and a national advisory board, and gives the agency's research and development office a mandate covering information science and technology among its research domains, empowering it to establish research, service, education and research-foundation institutions in the field. It is the strongest located foundation for domestic research capacity on digital questions. What the repository records happening under it is external: capacity workshops delivered by a regional economic commission

name: EriTel internet complaint form
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period
position_end: a live web form for internet-connectivity and web-application complaints operated by the state telecommunications provider, with telephone and email alternatives

subject: include.access
name: Refugee and displaced-person protection framework
status: Not held, no national framework and no convention accession
milestone: Guidance note supersedes the 2011 eligibility guidelines
position_end: The refugee agency's consolidated legal and governance profile records that the country is not party to the refugee convention, its protocol or the regional refugee convention, has no national legal framework specifically addressing refugee or asylum-seeker protection, and hosts a population of 119 refugees. The displacement runs the other way: by December 2025 the agency was aware of over 679,000 refugees and asylum-seekers from the country worldwide, and its April 2026 guidance note supersedes eligibility guidelines dating from 2011. The children's rights committee records the state's position that it hosts no refugee, asylum-seeking or internally displaced children

subject: include.access
name: Terms of access to telecommunications services
milestone: Operator's published application requirements and tariffs
position_start: Not held
position_end: The state operator requires, for a fixed telephone line, a written request with address and contact number, a completed application form, a copy of the identity card and a one-time payment of 882 nakfa; fixed wireless service requires a service request letter and comparable documentation. Prepaid mobile recharge is sold in denominations of 110 and 330 nakfa, recharged by a dialled code, alongside published short codes for emergency and customer services. The identity-card requirement makes the national identity card a precondition of a telephone line, which is the one documented link in this repository between the identity credential and access to a service. No connection volume, waiting time or subscriber figure is published

subject: data.statistics
name: Fourth Round Eritrea Population and Health Survey (EPHS 2025)
milestone: NSO reports survey completion: 9,794 households, 405 enumeration areas, 98.4% household completion, CAPI digital collection
position_end: Completed across all six regions using Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing; ~400 tables across 20 chapters drafted; report writing, printing and dissemination scheduled for 2026; NSO also compiled 2023 national accounts and began 2024 national-accounts data collection
sources: 2026-05-08 Eritrea strengthens data systems with EPHS 2025 (UNDP)
note: Technical support from Mikro International Consultancy Service (Oslo) and UNECA, under the UNDP-led Joint Programme on Data for Development (D4D); Eritrea's most concrete data-systems development on record

subject: data.statistics
name: National accounts methodology and database capacity
position_end: A two-week training in January 2026 delivered to the national statistics office covered national accounts compilation of output by the production approach under the 2008 international standard, and deployment of a national accounts database system. It strengthens the statistical system's methodology and database infrastructure. There is no statistics law in force under which any of it sits: a draft statistical proclamation was recorded pending in 2007 and no later enactment has been located

subject: data.open
name: Survey data produced for policy use
milestone: Case study on the national population and health survey
position_end: The government-led population and health survey of 2025, the first such national survey in fifteen years, was led by the statistics office and the health ministry with an international agency covering half of a US$535,000 budget. It is a nationally representative household data-collection exercise intended to close disaggregated-data gaps used for policy and development-goal tracking. Its report was scheduled for 2026 and no dataset, licence or open publication of it is held: data produced for development here means data produced for the state's own use

subject: data.satellite
name: Satellite-derived climate and rainfall monitoring
milestone: Regional climate advisory addressed to the country
position_end: The country's own delegation statement to the desertification convention lists setting up a modern national meteorological service among its forward strategies, which places a modern service as a planned objective rather than an operating institution; what exists is fragmented across a civil aviation meteorological service and an agricultural meteorology unit. The satellite-derived monitoring that does cover the country is produced abroad: a food agency dataset of dekadal rainfall indicators computed from satellite precipitation imagery blended with station data and short-term forecasts, aggregated to subnational units and refreshed roughly every two weeks; and a regional climate centre advisory of August 2026 using precipitation index analysis and satellite-derived soil-moisture and vegetation-stress monitoring to raise alert levels and forecast below-normal rainfall over the west of the country

subject: geopol.usa
name: United States engagement
milestone: Foreign minister meets a senior adviser at the assembly
position_end: The first substantive bilateral engagement of the window: the foreign minister met the United States president's senior adviser for African affairs at the general assembly in September 2025, discussing renewed engagement including trade, investment, infrastructure, transportation, communication and security partnerships. No hyperscaler, cloud provider or technology company engagement of any kind is held, and the external investment-climate assessment records the investment centre dormant and the investment law effectively suspended

subject: geopol.china
name: Belt and Road cooperation memorandum
position_end: The Chinese planning commission's own press release records the founding instrument: a memorandum on cooperation within the belt and road framework, signed on 24 November 2021 by the Chinese ambassador and the foreign minister. It is the standing framework, reaffirmed at leader level since. No digital, telecommunications or data project under it is named on the repository

subject: geopol.eu
name: European Union commitments and the documentation centre
position_end: No bilateral digital-transformation memorandum with the European Union is held. The instrument carrying its commitments is the partnership agreement signed in November 2023 and applied provisionally from January 2024, which lists the state among its parties and carries provisions on digital solutions for public access to information and on accelerating electronic governance and digital services. The clearest engagement in the window is a programme rather than an announcement: successive European funding with an Italian university as technical partner has equipped the research and documentation centre for digitisation, turning it into a digital-preservation centre with hands-on training capacity, and linked to a draft national archives and libraries law

subject: geopol.gulf
name: Gulf-state cooperation instrument
position_end: A general cooperation agreement between the foreign minister and a Saudi minister of state, signed in October 2010, covering diverse sectors. It is the principal ongoing Gulf-state relationship and the actual signed instrument that a February 2026 meeting with a Saudi deputy foreign minister agreed to expedite the implementation of. No dedicated Gulf digital-transformation, telecommunications or data-governance memorandum was located

subject: geopol.india
name: India's tele-education and tele-medicine network memorandum
position_end: The memorandum joining India's tele-education and tele-medicine network project, successor to the earlier pan-African network, is India's principal technology-delivery instrument with the country: tele-education and tele-medicine over India-built portals with an on-site learning centre equipped with computers, internet connection and audio-visual equipment. It is the clearest signed dated technology instrument between the two, and no India-Eritrea data-governance or digital public infrastructure instrument was located
